articleTitle: Techno-Economic Analysis and Optimization of Solar Energy System for Power Generation and Hydrogen Production in Al Mazyouna Area
publicationTitle: 2022 3rd International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: In this paper, a hybrid energy system using only renewable resources with hydrogen energy storage is proposed for Al-Mazyouna site which is located west of Dhofar governorate. The modeled system is investigated from techno-economic side using HOMER Pro Software. Real load data and solar radiation of Al Mazyouna were utilized in the modelling approach. The aim of this study to investigate the possibility of replacing diesel power plant, in this remote area, with renewable energy system and battery/Fuel cell system. The study considers three scenarios, PV system with battery, PV system with fuel cell and PV system with fuel cell-Battery. The optimal size of the system is based on the lowest value for the net present cost and the cost of energy. It was found that replacing the diesel generators with battery bank and PV system is possible but the cost of energy will increase from 0.188 US$/kWh to 0.422 US$/kWh but the main advantageous is that there will be no emission of harmful gases. Furthermore, replacing the battery bank by fuel cell with PV system is also possible, however, the cost of energy will further increase to 0.731 US$/kWh due to investment cost of electolyser, hydrogen tank and fuel cell. The main advantageous is that the Hydrogen fuel has high energy storage capacity and can store energy for longer time compared with battery bank in off-grid energy system. Combining two storage systems (Battery and Fuel cell) with PV resulted in energy cost reduction to 0.501 US$/kWh.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation Implementation of All-DC Offshore Wind Power System
publicationTitle: 2022 3rd International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: With the continuous advancement of the goal of “carbon neutrality” and “carbon peaking”, renewable energy sources such as solar energy, wind energy, and hydropower have developed rapidly. Compared with onshore wind power, offshore wind power has natural advantages such as abundant wind energy resources and no land occupation. However, due to the charging current of submarine cables, the traditional AC transmission method is only suitable for short-distance, small-capacity offshore wind farms. For this reason, full DC offshore wind power technology came into being. This paper analyzes and studies the principle of the high-voltage direct current transmission system of the offshore wind farm. In the full direct current offshore wind power system designed in this paper, the low-voltage alternating current generated by the wind turbine is converted into low-voltage direct current through a diode rectifier bridge and further passed through the isolated DC-DC converter, the low-voltage direct current is converted into high-voltage direct current and be transmitted using submarine cables. To effectively adjust the voltage of the DC transmission system, we use a proportional-integral controller to close-loop control the phase shift angle of the DC-DC converter. Next, the high-voltage DC power is converted into a civil AC power distribution system by the onshore inverter, and the output AC power is adjusted in real-time by the integral controller. Finally, the correctness and effectiveness of the proposed control method are verified by building the corresponding simulation model in Matlab/Simulink.

articleTitle: Carbon Emission Prediction with Macroeconomic Variables and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2022 3rd International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: Carbon Emission Prediction is important because China is the world's largest emitter of carbon, and an analysis of the factors affecting China's carbon emissions will help the country to save energy and reduce emissions in the future. This problem has been studied in the literature with 9 methods and 9 kinds of data. Most of the data were collected in the National Bureau of Statistics of China. We predict carbon emission with 44 Macroeconomic Variables and 7 machine learning models, with data from 31 provinces in China from 2011 to 2019. This study uses machine learning algorithms to discuss the impact of macroeconomic indicators in the dataset on carbon emissions in China. We found AdaBoost model is the most precise and Coal consumption variables are more important in the prediction.

articleTitle: Comparison of Medium-Term Load Forecasting Methods (Splitted Linear Regression and Artificial Neural Networks) in Electricity Systems Located in Tropical Regions
publicationTitle: 2022 3rd International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: Load forecasting for the medium term to supply power plants within 1 month, can optimize the economic dispatch of generators that will be used to supply large systems. The accuracy of forecasting the half-hourly load will result in a more efficient electricity supply in a system that uses flat rates on the utility side. In this paper, the author tries to compare the forecasting methods of linear regression, Artificial Neural Networks, and Splitted Linear Regression. This method is applied to the largest system in Indonesia, a country located at the tropical region which has different characteristics from countries that have four seasons. At the end of this study, it can be concluded that the Splitted Linear Regression method has the highest performance with the lowest MAPE value of 2.63%.

articleTitle: Method of Market Participation for Wind/Photovoltaic/ Energy Storage Based on KKT Condition
publicationTitle: 2022 3rd International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: With the development of renewable energy, the participation of renewable energy together with energy storage in electricity market has become an inevitable choice. The transaction strategy of renewable energy and energy storage has been studied extensively. However, most existing literature regards renewable energy and energy storage as price takers and ignores their impact on market operation. Therefore, in this paper, the equilibrium between electricity market and wind/photovoltaic/energy storage is investigated. A bi-level model considering the market clearing and the operation of wind/photovoltaic/energy storage is proposed. On the upper level, there is a market operation model, which aims to minimize the market operation cost. On the lower-level, there is a wind/photovoltaic/energy storage operation model, which aims to maximize the profits of wind/photovoltaic/energy storage. Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) condition is used for solving high computational complexity of bi-level model. The model at lower-level is transformed into constraints and put in the upper-level, thereby making the bi-level model become single-level. Then the problem is turned into a linear programming and it can be solved readily. Numerical case based on IEEE system demonstrates that the method we develop can effectively make the accommodation rate of renewable energy higher, improve the benefits of wind/photovoltaic/energy storage and reduce the market operation cost.

articleTitle: Effect of MPPT Technique in Solar System Efficiency: A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2022 3rd International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: Worldwide energy demand is growing fast because of the population explosion. Technological advancement paved the way toward utilizing renewable energy sources instead of fossil fuels as they cause harmful effects on the environment. Among all renewable sources, solar energy is a promising source. Solar energy is captured by photovoltaic (PV) arrays that convert the sunlight into electricity that powers the load. A vital component in the PV system is the DC-DC converter. Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) techniques can be applied to the DC-DC converter to deliver maximum power from the PV array. Thus, the efficiency of the PV system increases. This paper compares the output of a PV system with and without applying MPPT techniques. The PV system installed at Effat university library's rooftop is considered a case study in this paper. Matlab/Simulink software is used for simulation. The results show that applying MPPT leads to a more significant PV power. The output PV power when applying MPPT has an efficiency of 99.93%, and when there is no MPPT, the output power has an efficiency of 21.21%. Also, the power, voltage, and current waveforms in the system with MPPT achieved less harmonic distortion than the system without MPPT

articleTitle: Evaluating the Green and High Reliability Performance of Smart Distribution Networks by Applying Fuzzy Comprehensive Analysis Method
publicationTitle: 2022 3rd International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: Under the double-carbon target, smart distribution network (SDN) is the important direction of the future distribution system development. Scientific and reasonable evaluation for the SDN can effectively support its sustainable and healthy development. Thus, a new evaluation methodology based on multi-criteria decision making (MCDM) was proposed in this paper to reflect the comprehensive performance for SDN. The green development and high reliability for SDN were considered to select the evalution critertia. An evaluation index system was builded from the four perspectives of green developement, reliability, economy, technology and power quality. Considering the uncertainty of index value and subjectivity of decision-making, an integrated evaluation model was proposed based on improved entroy weight method and fuzzy VIKOR method. Four SDN alternatives was chosen as an empirical analysis to demonstrate the feasibility of the evaluation system.

articleTitle: Policy Assessment of Net Metering: The Case of Medium Voltage Industrial Consumer in Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2022 3rd International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: The use of clean energy source in industrial sector becomes important due to carbon tax policy. This policy will affect the price of the industrial product due to the additional charge of emissions generated by fossil source. Solar PV Net Metering (NEM) is one of the industrial consumer strategies to avoid carbon tax. Moreover, NEM is used to incentivize the distributed generation owner to promote clean energy. Aim of this work is to evaluate Indonesia net metering policy from large medium voltage industrial consumer's and utility company point of view. In this study, exported energy from large industrial prosumer is evaluated based on existing net metering policy by some simulation and scenarios based on real case. The result shown Indonesia latest NEM policy has not been able to give both side optimal benefit. Capacity charge rules affecting export electricity from prosumer to grid unable to reduce electricity bills. Capacity charge calculation need to re-formulated. From utility side, NEM cause rising number of excess power and increasing cost of the system due to addition of reserve margin cost and not sold energy.

articleTitle: Aerodynamic Design and Assessment of a Wind Turbine
publicationTitle: 2022 3rd International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: Wind energy is a relatively accessible clean energy that has a high conversion efficiency and development potential. However, wind turbines have a higher requirement in design than other energy generation methods. In order to attain the structure of an optimum blade design, techniques such as Blade element theory and the Betz model help us calculate the ideal length and shape of wind blades under certain environments. Compared to onshore wind turbines, offshore wind turbines achieve a larger wind speed and higher environmental stability. In this essay, we would choose an offshore location and conduct basic aerodynamic design procedures to obtain the parameters of an ideal wind turbine and calculate the energy yield of the turbine.

articleTitle: An Architecture to Negotiate and Monitor Energy Exchanges in the Smart Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2022 3rd International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: Traditional electrical power sources and their long distribution networks can no longer cope with the ever-increasing need for energy. Distributed energy generation in close geographical proximity to the consumption point is an alternative approach to energy provisioning. The complexities introduced by this approach require an advanced management system. The smart microgrid addresses this need. A second need identified in developing regions is for a management system that is both affordable and non-proprietary. This paper presents a smart microgrid architecture, based on open-source platforms, that addresses these needs. The architecture is explained by means of a use case. A database design is given with tables to reflect the contracts and associated energy exchanged between producers, consumers, and energy store devices.

articleTitle: Modification of BiOX by Sulfur Doping and Bismuth Deposition and Its Treatment of Drilling Fluid Polymers and Heavy Metals
publicationTitle: 2022 3rd International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: To solve the problems of secondary pollution and high cost caused by the traditional treatment of drilling fluid system. In this paper, a novel photocatalytic material S-Bi/BiOBr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</inf>Cl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</inf> was synthesized by hydrothermal method. The chemical states of elements on the surface were analyzed by x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). The morphology and structure of the samples were characterized by SEM and TEM. Through the RhB degradation experiment, it was shown that the material has good photocatalytic performance. The COD removal rate of the several common polymers in drilling fluid were more than 69%; The reduction rate of heavy metal ions in drilling fluid(lead nitrate, mercury nitrate, potassium dichromate and chromium sulfate) were 12.6%, 38.1%, 88.25% and 92.25%, respectively.

articleTitle: Experimental Study on the Behaviors of Continuous Liquid Spill Fire with an Obstacle
publicationTitle: 2022 3rd International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: Liquid fuel spill fires represent fire hazard in many applications spanning from industrial plant accidents wielding combustible liquids to residential fires involving flammable fuels. In this paper, spill fire experiments with n-butanol were conducted on steel trench with different square cylinder obstacle sizes (None, 3 cm, 5cm, and 7 cm) and discharge rates (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$100 \mathbf{ml}/\boldsymbol{\min\sim 700\text{ml}/\min})$</tex>. The burning and spreading behaviors including flame height, temperature near the obstacle, were recorded and analyzed. The results indicated that the flame height 2 cm downstream of the obstacle was decreases with the increasing obstacle size. The temperature and radiation near the obstacle also decrease with the increasing obstacle size. The heat absorbed by obstacle and convection by the flowing fuel were mainly responsible for this phenomenon.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Dual-Axis Solar Tracking Crystalline Silicon and Fixed-Plate Copper Indium Gallium Selenide Photovoltaic Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 3rd International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: The application of photovoltaic (PV) solar farms to complement the power generation of fossil fuel power plants has been constantly on the rise in the field of sustainable electricity generation. The solar energy is abundant and environmental-friendly. One of the most commonly installation of PV farms is fixed plate structure with crystalline Silicon (c-Si) panels. However, improving the solar to electrical energy conversion and optimizing the applications of PV farms have always been an ardent interest for researchers and PV applicants, thus several alternatives have been attempted. In this paper, the performance of two alternative PV installations over a period of 3 months was analyzed and compared with the fixed-plate c-Si PV farm. One of the PV farms was made up of thin film material - Copper Indium Gallium Selenide (CIGS) which is well-known for its light weight and flexibility features. The other PV farm was an open looped dual-axis solar tracker system which enhanced the efficiency of the PV system power generation by tracking the sun solar path. The 3 systems were analyzed and compared on several parameters such as the performance ratio, weight per <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{m}^{2}$</tex>, and efficiency per <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{m}^{2}$</tex>. The CIGS PV farm has the lightest weight in terms of per <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{m}^{2}$</tex> and per Wp, making it very suitable for Building-Integrated Photovoltaic (BIPV). The dual-axis tracker has excellent performance ratio and efficiency per <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{m}^{2}$</tex> as compared to the other 2 systems, however, it is the heaviest, requires maintenance and safety distance due to the extra structure and motors.

articleTitle: Development and Evolution of Energy Internet and Its Impact on Power System
publicationTitle: 2022 3rd International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: Recent years witness certain progress in both theory and practice of energy Internet. However, with the proposal of new strategies such as carbon dioxide peaking, carbon neutrality and new power systems, the connotation, characteristics and framework of energy Internet will undergo new evolution. This paper analyzes the basic characteristics of energy Internet from the perspectives of industrial chain, technical characteristics and market mechanism, depicts the evolution process of energy Internet market from micro-level to multi-market level. Three types of products and three transaction modes are proposed for energy Internet transactions and the impact of energy Internet on the traditional power system is analyzed from the perspectives of planning and market operation.

articleTitle: Transformation of KDO/KME System in Power Station
publicationTitle: 2022 3rd International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: The test data acquisition and processing system (KDO) and nuclear island test instrument system (KME) of No. 1/2 unit from Qin No. 2 Plant have been installed, commissioned and operated for more than 15 years. With the increase of operating years, the boards, power supplies and other equipment in the cabinet have been seriously aged, affecting the performance of the relevant test equipment and the monitoring and analysis of specific parameters. Starting from the perspective of technological transformation, this paper deeply analyzes the entire transformation process, and sorts out the difficulties one by one from equipment selection to technical transformation implementation. Then, through the use of a series of human error prevention tools, the smooth progress of each node in the transformation is ensured, so that the transformation can be completed within a short construction period of the overhaul. Then, the paper summarizes the transformation experiences to provide transformation experience for other power plant system transformation (especially selection of new technology).

articleTitle: Microstructure Analysis of Multilayer Graphene Reinforced Flake Titanium Composites
publicationTitle: 2022 3rd International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: Different multilayer graphene reinforced flake titanium matrix composite mixed powders were prepared by high energy ball milling. MLG / flake Ti composites were prepared by low temperature and high voltage discharge plasma sintering (SPS) and heat treated at high temperature (950°C). Flake Ti powders with different multilayer graphene (MLG) distribution were obtained by controlling the ball milling process parameters. The effects of MLG content and high temperature heat treatment time on the microstructure were studied. It is found that the proportion of flakes increases gradually with the extension of ball milling time. Through the observation of SPS preform, it is found that the lamella is basically perpendicular to the sintering pressure direction, forming an obvious layered structure. The mixture of titanium chips and MLG is distributed around the titanium lamella, forming an obvious interface, and there are a large number of needle like substances on the surface of the titanium lamella.

articleTitle: The Game of Three Oligopolies in China's Power Market in the Context of the Opening of the National Carbon Emission Trading Market
publicationTitle: 2022 3rd International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: This paper modifies the cost function from an old model according to the latest news that the national carbon emissions trading market opened in China, and then applies the new model to the Chinese power market in order to find out what impact the news has on three firms' output decisions. This paper tries to find new output equilibrium with new model and confirm the range of parameters that make the yield stable. The new model is about the dynamical system of three oligopolistic power firms under different expectations. This paper studies the existence and stability of the equilibrium point. The results of numerical simulations illustrate the complex behavior of the power firm game when the two-parameter changes and control the market chaos using the time-lag feedback method. The stability of the Nash equilibrium point relies heavily on the adjustment rate of finite rational players. Adaptive expectation of power companies' positive feedback to the market is conducive to market stability, while too small a feedback rate will lead the market into chaos. This paper concludes that government intervention has a positive impact on electric utilities. In addition, this paper expects to provide a basis for yield decisions for power companies considering the opening of the national carbon emission trading market.

articleTitle: Multi-Stage Optimization Model for New Power System Based on the Data Mining Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2022 3rd International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: The construction of a new power system with new energy as the mainstay is conducive to accelerating the green transformation of the economy and society and high-quality development. However, in the new power system, the new load spiking characteristics are obvious, and the increase in peak-to-valley difference on the load side will cause a greater impact on the traditional power system. To achieve the goal of building a new power system with new energy as the mainstay, the demand response potential of users needs to be fully explored, and to a certain extent, the demand side will be prompted to provide equivalent regulation resources to the power side, which is of great significance to alleviate the tension between power supply and demand and promote the consumption of renewable energy. Therefore, this paper develops a multi-stage optimization model for new power system based on data mining algorithms. The model is based on a cluster mining method to extract the typical electricity consumption behaviour characteristics of users. Then the demand response potential of multi-cluster customers is analysed and the demand response characteristics of multi-cluster customers are studied. Finally, a multi-stage demand response optimization model under the new power system is established.

articleTitle: Recent Developments of Solid-State Electrolytes for All-Solid-State Lithium Metal Batteries
publicationTitle: 2022 3rd International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: With the rapid popularization and development of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs), a series of challenges concerning the safety issues and the limited capacity of LIBs has drawn increasing attention. To address these challenges, all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs) with the solid-state electrolytes (SSEs), which have demonstrated high energy density and high safety, are expected to grow as next-generation power source for electric vehicles to replace conventional LIBs. This paper reviews the progress of SSE techniques, including inorganic, polymer and composite solid electrolyte systems. The advantages and limitations of these SSEs were further discussed with the summarization and comments about the preparation and modification techniques, as well as their applications and enhancements in ASSB. By giving a systematic introduction to the existing popular solid electrolyte strategies, the perspectives about the challenges and developments for the practical applications of SSEs are also proposed. The technology of SSEs reveals high promising future and great potential to reshape the power sources of electric vehicles.

articleTitle: Formal Verification of Fault Isolation and Restoration Algorithms in Smart Grid
publicationTitle: 2022 3rd International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: The efficacy of smart grid based modern power systems is primarily dependent on two way communication mechanisms for fault isolation and restoration of the grid. These systems are of critical nature and also have direct impact on customers in terms of down time. Many algorithms for effective fault restoration have been proposed. However, the requirement of physical testing of these algorithms against all possible cases has been a bottleneck for their timely deployment. To overcome this challenge, we propose a formal quantitative analysis in this paper. We argue that if we can formally model these algorithms, which can incorporate the randomness of the faults, then their verification can be reduced to the validation of their formal properties. To facilitate this process, we have identified a set of functional properties based on the working description of a given fault restoration algorithm. These properties are represented using the Linear Temporal Logic (LTL) operators that are available in PRISM, which is a probabilistic model checker. For illustration purposes, we use the PRISM model checker to model and analyze a real-world scenario of fault isolation and restoration while considering some key factors, like capacity of substations, fault occurrence at different load locations and efficient load balancing among substations.

articleTitle: An Analysis of Cadmium Telluride and Amorphous Silicon PV Cells
publicationTitle: 2022 3rd International Conference on Clean and Green Energy Engineering (CGEE)
abstract: Environmental concerns and global energy demands are pressuring the world to develop and utilize more clean energy sources, and solar photovoltaics (PV) is one of those technologies that has been in use by firms and countries around the globe. Solar PV can achieve the feat of zero emissions and operate for a long time at a substantial efficiency. Within this field of technology, different materials are being experimented with to improve the practicality of PV cells further. This article will compare amorphous silicon (a-Si) and cadmium telluride (CdTe) as materials for solar panels through various aspects. This paper will address the historical development, physical principles, implementations, system operation, environmental assessment, and economic evaluation of these cells. This work examines recent scholarly articles (i.e. background research, data analysis) that conclude that amorphous silicon technology has been refined to temporarily allow more frequent use than the toxic cadmium telluride cells.
